resources.string: Write Amharic with English letters: type selam and get ሰላም. Everything works offline. Nothing you type leaves your phone.
Turn on Hohe in your keyboard settings
Android shows a standard warning that keyboards can collect what you type. Hohe has no ads, no analytics and no internet use for typing.
Hohe isn\'t your current keyboard yet.

Type the English letters you use (for example: dexter) and the Amharic word you want (ደክስተር). It will be suggested first.
This data stays on your phone. Saved Amharic words and settings are included in your Android backup; nothing else is.
All settings go back to their defaults. Your words and clipboard are kept.

Make sure the key next to space shows a green bar and the space bar says አማርኛ. Type the word with English letters, like selam. The first suggestion (ሰላም) is typed when you press space. Tap another suggestion to pick it.
How do I switch to English?
Tap the ሕ key next to space. Hold it to see all typing styles.
A word I need isn\'t suggested
Hohe always offers a letter-by-letter version (underlined with dots). Pick it once and Hohe remembers it. You can also add the word under Settings, Typing, Saved Amharic words.
How do I type ። and other Ethiopic punctuation?
In Amharic mode, hold the . key. ብር is on the $ key in the symbols page.
Does Hohe send what I type anywhere?
No. Suggestions are computed on your phone. Hohe does not use the internet for typing and has no ads or analytics.
How do I move the cursor or delete words fast?
Slide your finger along the space bar to move the cursor. Swipe left from backspace to delete whole words.

Hohe is a keyboard that works offline. It does not collect, send or sell what you type. Words you pick, English words you type, your clipboard and recent emojis are stored only on this phone so suggestions can improve; you can clear them at any time under Clear data. Clipboard items expire after 24 hours unless pinned, and items marked sensitive (such as passwords) are never saved. Nothing is learned in password fields or private (incognito) fields. Voice typing uses your phone\'s speech service; Hohe only receives the recognised text. Settings and saved Amharic words are included in your Android backup.

Hohe is built with AndroidX and Jetpack Compose (Apache License 2.0) and Kotlin (Apache License 2.0). The English word list comes from the Android Open Source Project (Apache License 2.0). The Amharic word list is derived from Amharic Wikipedia text (CC BY-SA 4.0). Emoji names come from Unicode CLDR (Unicode License v3).
Voice typing uses your phone\'s speech recognition service in Amharic (am-ET) or English. Hohe needs microphone access to start it. Tap the microphone in the keyboard toolbar to speak.
Microphone allowed. Tap the mic in the keyboard to speak.

Handwriting is not part of this version of Hohe. It needs an on-device recognition model that must be downloaded from Google, and we will only add it with a clear opt-in. Type Amharic with English letters or use voice typing for now.
